messages.subject: ggplot map legend
parts:
I am making choropleths of the US and am trying to bucket a continuous variable associated with each state into just a handful of values.  For example, the value might be population of the state and I am trying to put it into 3 buckets: small, medium and large.  I pass the population to quantile and then cut in order to get my buckets, like this:

library(maps);
library(ggplot2);

states_map <- map_data("state");

raw_data      = sample(10000000:100000000,nrow(states_map),replace=T);
bucket_levels = quantile(raw_data, probs=seq(0, 1, .2));
# use digi.lab = 10 here to avoid scientific notation
bucket_data   = cut(raw_data, breaks = bucket_levels, include.lowest = T, dig.lab = 10);
ggplot(states_map, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(aes(fill = bucket_data), color = "white", size = 0.2) +
  scale_color_brewer() +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels=comma);

My problem is with the legend.  As the comment says, I use digi.lab = 10 to avoid scientific notation (the first problem). 

I have spent a few hours trying to solve 3 problems that I am hoping the list can help me with:
  1.  I want the labels to have commas (eg. "(123,123, 123,123,123]" instead of "(123123, 123123123]").
  2.  The labels sometimes have fractions, despite the data not having fractions.  (I'm mapping populations :)
  3.  I do not know how to modify the legend title (in this case "bucket_data"). 

Thanks!

I think it will be easier to format the labels when you cut, something like

bucket_data <- cut(raw_data,

labels = paste(
"(",
format(bucket_levels[1:(length(bucket_levels)-1)],
big.mark=","),
", ",
format(bucket_levels[-1],
big.mark=","),
"]",
sep = ""));

> 2. The labels sometimes have fractions, despite the data not having
> fractions. (I'm mapping populations :)
Also solved by setting your own labels in cut()

> 3. I do not know how to modify the legend title (in this case
> "bucket_data").

scale_fill_discrete("Scale name here")
